audit_items.proof_trace: `withdraw_underlying` (L306-316) enforces `cash >= cash_reserve.ceil()` on every explicit withdrawal, and all non-flash-loan withdrawal paths flow through it. However, `accrue_interest` (L124-149) increases `cash_reserve` by `reserve_factor * interest_accumulated` without updating `cash` and without asserting the invariant; in a high-utilization market (e.g., 95%+ of liquidity borrowed), sustained interest accrual can push `cash_reserve.ceil()` above `cash`, leaving the invariant violated. Any subsequent call to `withdraw_underlying` or `borrow_amount` will then abort — `borrow_amount` via integer underflow on `self.cash - self.cash_reserve.ceil()` and `withdraw_underlying` via assertion failure — freezing user withdrawals and new borrows until repayments restore `cash` above the threshold.
audit_items.attack_scenario: An attacker borrows nearly all available liquidity across multiple accounts (staying within the `borrow_amount` guard at the time of borrowing), then holds the positions while `accrue_interest` accumulates `cash_reserve` beyond the remaining `cash`; once `cash_reserve.ceil() > cash`, all other users' withdraw and borrow transactions revert, effectively freezing the market.
